text.title: Ramp Task Difficulty Ladder Worked Examples
text.summary: One complete five-rung `RampLadder` for a payments team after two ramps and a quarterly review that rewrote rung 3, with a note on every non-obvious value, and one bad ladder showing what the validator prints and what the tech lead sees beyond it.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: The payments-platform team hires four developers a year on a two-week ramp (10 working days). Dmytro joined on 2026-04-06 and reached rung 4; Iryna joined on 2026-05-11 and her rung-3 ticket (a refunds endpoint) ran 7 days against a 2-3 day band because it turned out to cross the ledger module. The tech lead (alice.m) runs the quarterly review on 2026-06-30.

example.title: payments-platform RampLadder 1.2.0 after the Q2 review
example.note: Every rung is a scope: one file with no flag at rung 1, one module behind a flag at rung 3, two modules with a design review at rung 4. No points, no sizes; a buddy can place a ticket by counting files and modules (r-rung-defined-by-observable-scope).
Upper bounds run 1, 2, 3, 5, 10: non-decreasing, rung 1 inside a day, rung 5 equal to the 10-day window (r-durations-monotonic-rung1-under-a-day).

Rung 1 evidence is PR #812 on the production payments repo, merged by the previous newcomer in 0.4 days; both ramps merged their first PR on day one, so the 3-day tolerance on `median_time_to_first_pr_days` holds (r-rung1-merges-to-main).
Support fades full pairing, pair on PR, review on PR, review on design, scheduled check-ins; nothing reads "none" (r-buddy-support-fades-per-rung).

Rungs 1-4 cite Dmytro's merged PRs with actual durations; rung 5 has never been completed by a newcomer, so it is `unvalidated` and its 5-10 band is a guess the next ramp will test (r-evidence-is-a-completed-prior-ramp).

Two tickets per rung were tagged 5-7 days before each start date; rungs 1 and 2 are off the critical path with no deadline in the window. PAY-2233 on the critical path is allowed at rung 3 and PAY-2241 with a deadline is allowed at rung 4, which is why those rungs are not day-one rungs (r-tickets-tagged-before-start-date).

Iryna's PAY-2230 ran 7 days against a 2-3 band, past twice the bound; it was reclassified to rung 4 (it crossed into ledger) rather than recorded as a slow newcomer, and she stayed on rung 3 at the end of the window (r-promotion-requires-completed-rung).

The review put rung 3's median at 4.75 days, outside its band for the first cycle, and rewrote the rung-3 pattern (modules_crossed_max stays 1, refunds-only examples) rather than widening the band; `version_bumped` is true and the ladder is 1.2.0. `next_due` is 92 days out, inside the quarterly cadence (r-outcome-review-regrades-rungs).

example.title: What the validator and the tech lead reject
example.note: Validator output: `$.rungs[0].name: matches forbidden 'not' schema`, `$.rungs[0].expected_duration_days.max: 2 violates maximum=1`, `$.rungs[0].tagged_tickets[0].on_critical_path: must equal False, got True`, `$.rungs[0].tagged_tickets[0].deadline_inside_ramp_window: must equal False, got True`, `$.rungs[1].name: matches forbidden 'not' schema`, `$.rungs[1].tagged_tickets: 1 items, minItems=2`, `$.rungs[2].evidence.not_applicable: missing required field`, `$.outcome_review.per_rung[0].action: 'none' not in enum ['rebanded', 'pattern_rewritten']`.

Once those are fixed, the cross-field block reports: `rungs[3]: buddy_support 'review_on_pr' is more support than the rung below; support only fades up the ladder (r-buddy-support-fades-per-rung)`, `rungs[4]: upper bound 12 exceeds ramp_window_days 10 (r-durations-monotonic-rung1-under-a-day)`, `rungs[4]: top rung buddy_support must be scheduled_check_ins, got 'review_on_design' (r-buddy-support-fades-per-rung)`, `ramps[0]: tickets tagged on 2026-05-12, after the start date 2026-05-11 (r-tickets-tagged-before-start-date)`, `ramps[0].progression[0]: 4 days is past twice rung 1's upper bound 1 and the ticket was not reclassified (r-promotion-requires-completed-rung)`, `ramps[0].progression[1]: rung 4 after rung 1; one merged ticket per rung, no skips (r-promotion-requires-completed-rung)`, `outcome_review: next_due 2027-01-15 is 199 days after last_run; quarterly cadence allows 92 (r-outcome-review-regrades-rungs)`, `outcome_review.per_rung[0]: rung 1 out of band for 2 cycles; a review that changes nothing is invalid (r-outcome-review-regrades-rungs)`.

What the tech lead sees beyond the validator: rung 1's evidence is a PR on the onboarding-kata repo, so nobody has proven the real clone-build-test-deploy path fits in a day; rung 2's evidence is the tech lead's own half-day PR, which says nothing about a newcomer; and Iryna, a senior hire, was handed the ledger migration on day five "because she is senior" and spent nine days reverse-engineering the deploy pipeline, which the review then recorded as her pace instead of a rung skip.
